concepts.name: Big-O notation
concepts.gloss: Asymptotic upper bounds on running time such as O(n log n).

concepts.name: Polynomials
concepts.gloss: Expressions Σ aₖ xᵏ with coefficients, their addition and multiplication.

concepts.name: Complex numbers
concepts.gloss: Numbers a+bi with i²=−1, with modulus, conjugate and unit-modulus phases e^{iθ}.

concepts.name: Multitape Turing machine
concepts.gloss: A machine with finitely many states, a finite alphabet and one-dimensional tapes whose heads move one cell per step.

concepts.name: Matrices, rank, subspaces and orthogonality
concepts.gloss: Matrices over a field, their rank, subspaces, orthogonal complements under a bilinear form, and tensor products of spaces.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Modular arithmetic and the Chinese remainder theorem
concepts.gloss: Arithmetic on residues mod q, units, inverses mod q, gcd, and the fact that coprime moduli split a residue ring into a product.

evidence.quote: Uniqueness follows from $\gcd(Q,c)=1$

concepts.name: Convolution and cyclic convolution
concepts.gloss: The product of two coefficient lists as polynomials; cyclic convolution wraps indices mod a length, so that it is multiplication in C[x]/(x^S−1).

evidence.quote:
Splitting the inputs into radix digits reduces multiplication to
convolution of short integer coefficients.

concepts.name: Discrete Fourier transform and the convolution theorem
concepts.gloss: The length-q transform (F_q u)_k = (1/q) Σ u_j e^{−2πi jk/q} built from roots of unity; it turns convolution into pointwise product and is inverted by the opposite-sign transform.

evidence.quote: (F_q u)_k=\frac1q\sum_{j=0}^{q-1}u_j e^{-2\pi i jk/q}

concepts.name: Butterfly and FFT recursion
concepts.gloss: The fast evaluation of a length-t transform by pairing entries z_k and z_{k+t/2}, applying a two-point butterfly, multiplying by twiddle roots and recursing on both halves.

evidence.quote:
the decimation-in-frequency step pairs $z_k$ with $z_{k+t/2}$ for
$0\leq k<t/2$

concepts.name: Multidimensional transform (tensor product)
concepts.gloss: A transform on an array indexed by several axes, equal to applying the one-dimensional transform along each axis in turn; convolution on a product of cyclic groups is diagonalised by it.

evidence.quote:
it replaces the Fourier transforms needed for
this convolution by multidimensional transforms whose axis lengths are
powers of two

concepts.name: The n log n optimality conjecture
concepts.title: The $n\log n$ optimality conjecture

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

concepts.gloss: Schönhage and Strassen's 1971 conjecture that n log n is the optimal order of multiplication cost on multitape Turing machines; the paper refutes any eventual Ω(n log n) lower bound for a fixed machine.

evidence.quote:
disproves the $n\log n$ optimality
conjecture of Sch\"onhage and Strassen in this model

concepts.name: The established O(n log n) multiplier as a subroutine
concepts.gloss: Harvey and van der Hoeven's existing O(N log N) integer multiplication, called as an ordinary black box on shorter records (not the improved algorithm).

evidence.quote:
Calls to the established $O(n\log n)$ multiplier are ordinary subroutine
calls; they do not invoke the improved theorem recursively.

concepts.name: Fixed-point disk grid and truncation
concepts.gloss: Complex numbers of modulus at most 1 whose real and imaginary parts are multiples of 2^{−p}, stored as signed two's-complement numerators, with Q_p truncating toward zero.

evidence.quote: A disk array has norm at most one.

concepts.name: Contractions and error accumulation
concepts.gloss: A linear map is a contraction if it does not increase the maximum-modulus norm; approximate algorithms for contractions compose with errors that add.

evidence.quote:
Composing such algorithms
adds their errors

concepts.name: Exact Gaussian dyadic arithmetic and guard bits
concepts.gloss: Intermediate values with power-of-two denominators are kept exact by allocating extra integer and fractional guard bits, and rounded only once after a whole layer.

evidence.quote:
Intermediate values are exact Gaussian dyadics,
whose real and imaginary parts have power-of-two denominators.

concepts.name: Arrays, addresses, rows and volume on tape
concepts.gloss: Arrays with multi-field addresses stored in lexicographic order on a tape, with address fields, row fields, prefix and suffix, spectator fields and logical volume V in bits.

evidence.quote:
An array with address set $[a_1]\times\cdots\times[a_t]$ is stored in
lexicographic order, with the first coordinate most significant.

concepts.name: Elementary stream operations
concepts.gloss: Linear-time tape scans: permuting two digit positions, moving a digit, splitting into streams and merging, and splitting whole rows cyclically into W streams.

evidence.quote:
Each of the following operations on an array of
volume $V$ takes $O(V)$ steps on a fixed number of one-dimensional tapes

concepts.name: Controlled shifts
concepts.gloss: Updating a later address field by an offset computed from earlier fields (y ↦ y+a mod q^b), or multiplying it by a rational unit, in linear time.

evidence.quote:
The next operations are linear because their target field follows their
control fields.

concepts.name: Row splitting among roles with padding
concepts.gloss: Distributing whole rows cyclically among the W wire roles, after padding the row count to a multiple of a power of W, so each role stream has volume V/W.

evidence.quote:
Distribute rows cyclically among the $W$ roles, padding the row count
for each prefix to a multiple of $W$.

concepts.name: Depth-first recursion on fixed tapes
concepts.gloss: Running recursive calls with finitely many tapes by parking inactive role streams on a stack tape, copying the active one to the child, and restoring afterwards, at cost linear in the parent's volume.

evidence.quote:
Reserve $W$ role tapes, a fixed set of
I/O and elementary-operation work tapes, one parking stack tape, and a
separate descriptor stack.

concepts.name: Linear network with roles and restored scratch
concepts.gloss: A fixed network of linear gates on wires (roles) that exchanges two banks of values with signs while restoring every auxiliary (scratch) wire whatever its initial contents.

evidence.quote:
Each procedure arises from its own fixed linear network that exchanges two
banks of values, with prescribed signs, and restores every auxiliary
value.

concepts.name: Three-subset gather, scatter and side-wire gadget
concepts.gloss: The scalar gadget on three-element subsets of [100]: copy, gather, scatter and side injection with intersection-size coefficients, scheduled in 8 rows so that y_S gains x_S independently of scratch values.

evidence.quote:
The construction uses
three-element subsets: gather and scatter create coefficients depending
on intersection size, and auxiliary wires cancel the unwanted
coefficients.

concepts.name: Frames and edge operators
concepts.gloss: Invertible operators D_v on a wire's address-indexed array attached to each network vertex; a common frame commutes with pointwise linear gates, so only edges D_v D_u⁻¹ need implementing and the endpoints determine the net operator.

evidence.quote:
We call $D_v$ its frame: the stored
array is $D_vg$ when the logical array is $g$.

concepts.name: Nested subspace labels and rank deficit
concepts.gloss: Nondegenerate subspaces of a fixed m-dimensional space attached to gates and terminals, nested along edges, so that the total dimension change s over all edges is strictly less than W·m, where W is the wire count.

evidence.quote:
The decisive property is that the total
number $s$ of smaller calls satisfies $s<Wm$.

concepts.name: Address shear interface
concepts.gloss: The endpoint operator of the bit network: fields H, D over a residue ring updated by (H,D) ↦ (H+MD,D), with matrices M at vertices whose differences give rank-many smaller interchanges per edge.

evidence.quote:
that endpoint operator is an address shear:
two fields, written as vectors $H,D$ over a common residue ring, are
updated by $(H,D)\mapsto(H+D,D)$

concepts.name: Lower triangular factorization and matrix shear cost
concepts.gloss: Every rational matrix factors as E₁ΠE₂ with E₁, E₂ lower triangular and Π a partial permutation with rank-many ones, so a shear by A costs rank(A) interchanges plus linear work.

evidence.quote: Every rational $m\times m$ matrix $A$ of rank $a$ has a factorization

concepts.name: Recursive power saving
concepts.gloss: When a size-mf call uses s calls of size f on streams of volume V/W with s<Wm, the normalized cost satisfies F_k ≤ (s/W)F_{k−1}+O(1), giving cost O(V e^τ) with τ<1 instead of a factor e.

evidence.quote:
After dividing cost by volume, multiplying the parameter by $m$
increases the recursive contribution by $s/W<m$. This strict inequality
is the source of the power saving.

concepts.name: Fast address-chunk interchange
concepts.gloss: The first tape procedure: swapping two disjoint u-bit address chunks of an array by recursion on the bit network in O(V u^τ) time for a fixed τ<1, intermediate steps computing XORs but the final effect an exact permutation.

evidence.quote:
The first procedure interchanges two disjoint contiguous address fields
of $u$ bits in an array whose addresses form a complete Cartesian
product. Its cost is $O(Vu^\tau)$ for a fixed $\tau<1$.

concepts.name: Butterfly kernel H₀ and phase kernel C
concepts.title: Butterfly kernel $H_0$ and phase kernel $C$

symbols.name: butterfly kernel
symbols.meaning: The two-point map (u,v) ↦ ((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) acting on a pair of complex values.

symbols.name: phase kernel
symbols.meaning: The 2×2 matrix aI+bX with a=(1+i)/2, b=(1−i)/2 that conjugates to the butterfly via phases.

concepts.gloss: The two-point butterfly H₀(u,v)=((u+v)/2,(u−v)/2) and the kernel C=aI+bX with a=(1+i)/2, b=(1−i)/2, related by H₀=b·S·C·S with S=diag(1,i), so a layer of H₀ equals phases times a layer of C.

evidence.quote: H_0(u,v)=\bigl((u+v)/2,(u-v)/2\bigr)
H_0^{\otimes D}=b^D\mathcal S_D C^{\otimes D}\mathcal S_D

concepts.name: Binary phase interface
concepts.gloss: The complex network with binary labels, in which each edge's frame change is a product of translation kernels aI+bX_v, one per residual basis vector, so that telescoping gives C⊗m on every role.

evidence.quote:
After source and sink diagonal corrections, and undoing the signed
bank exchange, telescoping these phase frames gives $C^{\otimes m}$
on every role, including auxiliary roles.

concepts.name: Packed selected-bit addition
concepts.gloss: XORing corresponding selected bits of two address chunks across many chunks at once, using a temporary third chunk, a few cyclic shifts, and a deterministic repair of a small exceptional set of addresses.

evidence.quote:
We implement a binary
row addition on corresponding selected bits in two
address chunks.

concepts.name: Simultaneous butterfly layer
concepts.gloss: The second tape procedure: applying H₀ at the same bit position in d address chunks of every record in O(V d^λ') time, evaluated exactly with guard bits and truncated once.

evidence.quote:
Each record is a polynomial with complex fixed-point coefficients, and
$H_0$ acts coefficientwise.

the cost is $O(Vd^{\lambda'})$ for a
fixed $\lambda'<1$

concepts.name: Polynomial ring modulo y^r + 1
concepts.title: Polynomial ring modulo $y^r + 1$

symbols.name: ring variable
symbols.meaning: The formal variable whose powers act as roots of unity in the ring.

symbols.name: record length
symbols.meaning: The number of complex coefficients in a polynomial record, a power of two.

concepts.gloss: The ring of complex polynomials of degree < r with y^r = −1; multiplication by a power of y is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

evidence.quote: one coordinate is stored as the coefficient list of a polynomial modulo $y^r+1$, with $r$ a power of two

concepts.name: Synthetic polynomial transform
concepts.gloss: A multidimensional transform over the ring mod y^r+1 whose roots of unity are powers of y, so twiddle multiplications are signed shifts and only butterflies cost arithmetic.

evidence.quote:
Powers of $y$ then
serve as roots of unity in the remaining axes, and multiplication by
such a root is a signed shift of the coefficient list.

concepts.name: Retained frequency order
concepts.gloss: Leaving transform outputs in the bit-reversed order the recursion writes them, so the pointwise product and the opposite transform consume that order without a separate permutation.

evidence.quote:
The two forward synthetic transforms
retain the same frequency order through their pointwise product

concepts.name: Transform layout for parallel layers
concepts.gloss: The tape layout that places the selected bits of the participating axes at a common offset in consecutive K-bit chunks, using bit moves and chunk interchanges, so each transform round is one simultaneous butterfly layer.

evidence.quote:
To apply Proposition~\ref{prop:simultaneous-layer} in a transform round,
we must place the selected bits of the participating axes at a common
offset in consecutive $K$-bit chunks.

concepts.name: Signed packing (Kronecker substitution)
concepts.gloss: Evaluating integer-coefficient polynomials at 2^{4p} to turn polynomial products into integer products, with signed carries and centered extraction of coefficients.

evidence.quote:
Signed coefficient
packing is a form of Kronecker substitution

concepts.name: Ring convolution from the retained transform layout
concepts.gloss: Normalized convolution over the ring: two forward synthetic transforms, pointwise ring products by signed packing, then the opposite transform, with error below √2 M(3ℓ+1)2^{−p}.

evidence.quote: Perform both forward transforms and retain their common $LB$ order.

concepts.name: Phase twist from cyclic to negacyclic
concepts.gloss: Multiplying coefficient k of the last cyclic axis by ζ^k with ζ=e^{πi/r} turns x^r−1 into y^r+1, so complex cyclic convolution is computed by ring convolution and the untwist.

evidence.quote:
A phase twist changes the last cyclic coordinate into a polynomial
modulo $y^r+1$

concepts.name: Gaussian resampling
concepts.gloss: Harvey–van der Hoeven's identity converting a Fourier transform of prime-ish length s into one of larger length t via Gaussian-weighted maps S and T, with a near-identity correction N.

evidence.quote:
Gaussian resampling
connects these two shapes.

concepts.name: Resampling with the permutations left in the transform
concepts.gloss: The paper's variant P_s F_s = 2^{2α²} B₀ P_t F_t A that keeps the coordinate permutations in the identity instead of executing two sorts per axis.

evidence.quote:
We retain both permutations in the transform formula and
compute that formula directly.

concepts.name: Bluestein chirp identity
concepts.gloss: Rewriting a transform as pointwise chirp phases around a cyclic convolution with a chirp kernel, which here also absorbs the target permutation.

evidence.quote:
Bluestein's chirp identity converts the middle transform,
including its target permutation, into normalized cyclic convolution.

concepts.name: Source permutation cancellation
concepts.gloss: The retained source permutation R cancels across two forward source transforms, their pointwise product and the opposite-sign transform, leaving (u*v)/S².

evidence.quote: the source permutation retained during resampling cancels

concepts.name: Chinese-remainder address map
concepts.gloss: An algebra isomorphism from cyclic convolution of length S=∏s_i (s_i pairwise coprime) to convolution on the product of cyclic axes, implemented by triangular controlled shifts.

evidence.quote:
used the Chinese remainder
theorem to convert one cyclic convolution into multidimensional cyclic
convolution

concepts.name: Integer product as radix-digit convolution
concepts.gloss: Writing both inputs in base 2^b with q digits, the integer product is the convolution of the digit lists; padding to length S exceeds the degree so no wraparound occurs and coefficients stay below 2^{3b}.

evidence.quote: Thus convolution modulo $x^S-1$ has no nonzero wraparound.

concepts.name: Parameter choices and padded box
concepts.gloss: The sizes p=6b, d=⌊b^ε⌋, K=⌊d^c⌋, T in [4n/b,8n/b), r=2^⌈(log₂T)/d⌉ and axis lengths t_i∈{r/2,r}, with α, γ, η and fixed rational exponents.

evidence.quote: Take the power of two $T$ in $[4n/b,8n/b)$

concepts.name: Prime source lengths
concepts.gloss: Distinct odd primes s_i in (1−2η)t_i < s_i ≤ (1−η)t_i near each power of two t_i, found by deterministic trial division, so that T/2<S<T and each ratio t_i/s_i leaves enough separation for resampling.

evidence.quote: The distinct prime lengths $s_i$ must be close to the powers of two

concepts.name: Source transform pipeline
concepts.gloss: The approximate source transform: resample with A along each axis, apply the chirp transform via ring convolution, compress with B₀, and rescale by 2^γ, equal to R F_s.

evidence.quote: computed chirp transform $\widetilde{\mathscr C}$

concepts.name: Exact recovery by scaling, rounding and carries
concepts.gloss: Removing the known normalizations S and 2^{2b+4}, proving the coefficient error is below 1/2, rounding to integers and propagating radix-2^b carries to the exact 2n-bit product.

evidence.quote:
proves that the recovered
coefficient error is strictly below $1/2$, and propagates carries to
obtain the exact binary product

concepts.name: The multiplication algorithm
concepts.gloss: The six steps: form radix digits, apply the address map Φ, compute two source transforms, multiply pointwise, apply the opposite transform, rescale, round and carry.

evidence.quote:
Apply the coefficient-address map $\Phi$, with its padded layout, to obtain
source arrays $u,v$.

concepts.name: Cost analysis and the exponent κ
concepts.title: Cost analysis and the exponent $\kappa$

symbols.name: power saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{-182} by which the logarithmic factor is reduced.

concepts.gloss: The table of normalized costs per Tp, each at most p^{1−2κ}, with the smallest margin 2^{−181}=2κ, giving total O(n (lg n)^{1−κ}) for κ=2^{−182}.

evidence.quote: Thus $\min_i g_i=2^{-181}=2\kappa$.

concepts.name: Integer multiplication in O(n (lg n)^(1−κ)) time
concepts.title: Integer multiplication in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ time

symbols.name: input length
symbols.meaning: The number of bits in each of the two integers being multiplied.

symbols.name: power saving exponent
symbols.meaning: The fixed constant 2^{-182} by which the logarithmic factor is reduced.

concepts.gloss: The main theorem: one deterministic fixed-alphabet, fixed-tape Turing machine multiplies n-bit integers in O(n(lg n)^{1−κ}) worst-case time, refuting the n log n conjecture, via synthetic transforms accelerated by the interchange and butterfly procedures.

evidence.quote:
We give a deterministic algorithm that multiplies two $n$-bit integers
in $O(n(\lg n)^{1-\kappa})$ worst-case time

concepts.name: Binary representation and schoolbook arithmetic
concepts.gloss: A nonnegative integer is written as a string of bits (or digits in base b) with the leftmost digit most significant, and addition and multiplication by hand take time quadratic in the length using carries.

concepts.name: Floor, ceiling and logarithms
concepts.gloss: The notations floor(x), ceiling(x), lg x = log_2 x and the iterated logarithm, together with the rule that an integer v needs floor(log_2 v)+1 bits.

concepts.name: Exponentials and elementary inequalities
concepts.gloss: Calculus-level facts on exponentials and powers with real exponents, limits, and simple inequalities such as 1+x <= e^x used to compare growth rates.

concepts.name: Summation, telescoping sums and geometric series
concepts.gloss: Finite sums written with Σ, sums in which consecutive terms cancel, and the closed form of geometric series.

concepts.name: Recurrences and the recursion tree
concepts.gloss: A cost T(n) defined in terms of smaller instances, solved by unrolling or a recursion tree to obtain a closed-form bound.

concepts.name: Karatsuba and classical multiplication algorithms
concepts.gloss: The schoolbook O(n^2) multiplication and Karatsuba's divide-and-conquer O(n^{log_2 3}) multiplication, as taught in algorithms courses, as the baseline against which faster methods are compared.

concepts.name: Recursion, call stack and subroutines
concepts.gloss: A procedure calling smaller instances of itself, with a stack of suspended calls, and the idea of using a procedure as a black box with a stated cost.

concepts.name: Sets, functions, bijections and permutations
concepts.gloss: Index sets such as [n]={0,...,n-1}, product sets, functions and their composition, and permutations as bijections of a finite set.

concepts.name: Mathematical induction and proof techniques
aliases: induction on the number of steps
concepts.gloss: Standard proof methods for correctness and cost claims: induction, contradiction, and invariants maintained across steps.

concepts.name: Prime numbers and trial division
concepts.gloss: A prime has no divisors besides 1 and itself; integers are uniquely products of primes; primality of small numbers can be found by dividing by all smaller candidates.

concepts.name: Groups, rings and fields
concepts.gloss: Basic abstract-algebra vocabulary: sets with addition and multiplication satisfying axioms, with fields (such as the rationals, the complex numbers and the two-element field F_2) allowing division, and cyclic groups Z/qZ.

concepts.name: XOR and arithmetic over F_2
concepts.gloss: The exclusive-or of two bits is their sum modulo 2, applied coordinatewise to bit strings, and is its own inverse.

concepts.name: Special matrices and matrix algebra
concepts.gloss: Matrix multiplication, inverses and transposes, and the identity, diagonal, permutation and triangular matrices, together with standard basis vectors e_j.

concepts.name: Triangle inequality and norm bounds
concepts.gloss: The modulus of a sum is at most the sum of moduli, used to bound approximation errors that add.

concepts.name: Rational numbers and dyadic fractions
concepts.gloss: Quotients of integers, and in particular numbers whose denominator is a power of two, which have finite binary expansions.

concepts.name: Deterministic algorithms and worst-case time
concepts.gloss: An algorithm with no randomness whose cost is the maximum number of steps over all inputs of a given length, with a single pass over input called linear time.

concepts.name: Entrywise operations on arrays and vectors
concepts.gloss: Operations applied independently to each coordinate of a list or multi-indexed array, and the identification of polynomials, vectors and arrays with coefficient lists.

background.summary: The reader has an undergraduate computer science education: discrete mathematics (sets, functions, induction, summations, recurrences, basic number theory and elementary group/ring/field vocabulary), an algorithms course (recursion, divide and conquer, schoolbook and Karatsuba multiplication, the FFT at the level of the divide-and-conquer recursion, solving recurrences), single-variable calculus (limits, exponentials, logarithms) and one course in linear algebra and complex numbers. They know Turing machines and big-O at an introductory level, but have not studied fast integer multiplication beyond Karatsuba, Schönhage-Strassen or Harvey-van der Hoeven, numerical error analysis, bilinear forms over finite fields, matrix factorizations such as Bruhat decompositions, or tape-level algorithm engineering.
